articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes of Chronic Anterior Dislocations Treated with Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Molokwu BO, Xu JJ, Myerson CL, Sultan T, Ben-Ari E, Zuckerman JD, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for chronic anterior shoulder dislocations or proximal humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 17 chronic dislocation patients matched to 51 proximal humerus fracture controls
articles.outcomes: Active forward elevation, external rotation, internal rotation, heterotopic ossification, complications, reoperations, and patient-reported outcomes including upper extremity function, pain interference and pain intensity
articles.take_home: Patients with chronic anterior shoulder dislocations treated with reverse total shoulder arthroplasty achieved similar shoulder movement to those treated for fractures, but reported lower overall function and more pain. Bone healing problems were more common in the dislocation group, though serious complications were rare in both groups.

articles.title: Comparing Inferiorized and Lateralized Glenospheres in Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty Using the LimaCorporate SMR Reverse Shoulder System: A Single-Center Analysis.
articles.authors: Pearsall C, Lachance A, Whittemore C, Neumann D, Choi J
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty with the LimaCorporate SMR Reverse Shoulder System
articles.sample_size: 460 patients (329 with inferiorized glenospheres, 131 with lateralized glenospheres)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates, patient-reported outcomes (ASES and VAS pain scores), mortality, and achievement of minimal clinically important difference at 6-12 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: There were no significant differences in reoperation rates, pain improvement, patient satisfaction, or survival between the two types of glenosphere design in this study. Both types of glenosphere performed comparably over the short term, though longer follow-up is needed to see if differences emerge later.

articles.title: Telerehabilitation-Based Motor Control Exercises After Rotator Cuff Surgery: Effects on Shoulder Function and Quality of Life.
articles.authors: Kocabay SY, Buker N, Yorukoglu AC, Sahin S, Ok N
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff surgery
articles.outcomes: Pain, shoulder range of motion, muscle strength, scapular positioning, shoulder function, fear of movement, and quality of life
articles.take_home: Adding motor control exercises via telerehabilitation to standard rehabilitation improved scapular positioning and shoulder muscle strength more than standard rehabilitation alone. Both groups improved with rehabilitation, but the motor control group showed better results for specific strength and movement measures.

articles.title: Revision risk of cross-linked versus non-crosslinked polyethylene in reverse shoulder arthroplasty: an analysis of 63,502 cases from the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Nguyen TQ, Gill DRJ, Corfield S, McCaul M, Cass B
articles.study_type: Observational registry analysis comparing implant types
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary reverse shoulder replacement for osteoarthritis, rotator cuff arthropathy, or fracture
articles.sample_size: 63,502 procedures (28,819 osteoarthritis, 24,779 rotator cuff arthropathy, 9,904 fracture)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery rates comparing highly cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) versus non-highly cross-linked polyethylene (non-XLPE) components, with infection as the most common reason for revision in non-XLPE cases
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacements using highly cross-linked plastic components had lower revision rates than standard plastic components, particularly in patients with osteoarthritis and rotator cuff arthropathy where infection-related revisions were more common with non-XLPE implants.

articles.title: Public Perceptions of Robotic-Assisted Shoulder Arthroplasty in the United States.
articles.population: Adults residing in the United States
articles.outcomes: Public perceptions of robotic-assisted shoulder arthroplasty, treatment preferences, factors associated with preference for robotic-assisted surgery
articles.take_home: Most people believe robot-assisted shoulder surgery gives better positioning and results than standard surgery, but 62% would still choose a very experienced surgeon without robots over a less experienced one with them. The main concerns are equipment failure, cost, and surgeon inexperience with the technology.

articles.title: Reliability of the Classification for Assessing Hand Behind the Back Following Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kinnair A, Ladermann A, Daniel C, Collin P
articles.study_type: Prospective observational cohort study validating a classification system
articles.population: Patients who had undergone reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 116 shoulders from 110 patients, mean age 70.7 years
articles.outcomes: Interobserver reliability of hand behind the back classification compared to vertebral-level method; association with functional outcome measures (Constant score, SST, ADLER, SSV)
articles.take_home: A new bedside classification system for assessing hand behind the back movement after reverse shoulder surgery is much more reliable and consistent than the traditional measurement method. This new approach also better reflects how well patients can perform everyday activities.

articles.title: Does Immobilization Method Make a Difference in Conservative Management of Proximal Humeral Fractures? A Prospective Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Sarikas DM, Kapicioglu DM, Sahin DK, Bilsel DK
articles.population: Patients with proximal humerus fractures treated conservatively
articles.sample_size: 105 patients (34 Velpeau bandage, 39 standard sling, 32 padded sling)
articles.outcomes: Subjective Shoulder Value, pain, ASES score, DASH score, Constant score, range of motion, nonunion and malunion rates
articles.take_home: The type of immobilisation device used to treat proximal humerus fractures makes no difference to how well patients recover or whether bones heal properly. The choice of immobilisation can therefore be based on what is most comfortable for the patient and what costs least.

articles.title: Migration patterns of the humeral component of the stemless Simpliciti Shoulder System in stemless anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty A radiostereometric and clinical study with 60-month follow-up.
articles.authors: de Bruin LJE, Brinke BT, Oomen R, Hoelen M, Hesseling B, Mathijssen N
articles.study_type: Prospective longitudinal cohort study with radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing stemless anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty with the Simpliciti Shoulder System
articles.outcomes: Humeral component migration patterns measured by model-based radiostereometric analysis; clinical outcomes including Constant-Murley Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, DASH score, and VAS; complications and implant survival
articles.take_home: The stemless shoulder implant remained stable from 2 to 5 years after surgery in most patients, with very small amounts of movement. Although 3 patients showed continued migration over this period, this did not affect their clinical outcomes or implant survival.

articles.title: Humeral Head Geometry: An Analysis of Global Offset against Intramedullary Shaft Diameter and Humeral Head Size: A CT Scan Study.
articles.authors: Lent-Koop J, Orbay J, Kelley N, Wells L, Heifner J, Saltzman M, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18-93 years with healthy shoulders
articles.outcomes: Humeral head diameter, medullary canal diameter, and global offset (distance between humeral head centre and shaft axis); relationships between these measurements assessed by age and sex
articles.take_home: Men have larger shoulder bones than women, but the position of the humeral head centre relative to the shaft varies independently of bone size and does not change with age. This positioning is important for designing shoulder replacement implants.

articles.title: Social determinants of health disparities are associated with lower total shoulder arthroplasty utilization and increased medical complications: A propensity-matched analysis.
articles.authors: Omurzakov AM, Omurzakov A, Oquendo Y, White AE, Dines JS, Fu MC, et al.
articles.study_type: Propensity-matched observational study using electronic health records
articles.sample_size: 84,767 patients per utilization cohort; 2,071 patients per complications cohort
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome was total shoulder arthroplasty utilization within 5 years. Secondary outcomes were 90-day and 1-year postoperative complications including emergency department visits, cardiac events, acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, and mechanical complications.
articles.take_home: Patients facing social and economic hardships were less likely to have shoulder replacement surgery for arthritis and had more medical complications after surgery. The findings suggest these differences reflect unequal access to care rather than problems with the surgery itself.
